span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Relegating state consciousness to a background condition screens off any contribution the state NCC makes to constituting a content's being conscious, so the design can only speak to which content is represented
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The pre-existing conscious state, not the induced content, may be the actual difference-maker that renders the content conscious
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The argument shows the current paradigms need re-development, not that no NCC can ever be found.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper is neutral between theories of consciousness and does not adjudicate them.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The design is argued to be flawed in the way a carcinogen study would be if every mouse already had the cancer: the property of interest is presupposed in every subject.
span.note: what this limits: a content-NCC result as evidence about what makes a content conscious: the design presupposes the property whose instantiation is at issue, exactly as a carcinogen study would if the property were already instantiated in all the mice
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On the author's own account the approach can at best deliver the conditions for a content being SELECTED for consciousness, which is a different question from a content being conscious.
span.note: what this limits: the content-based NCC literature: at best it finds the minimally sufficient conditions for selection into consciousness, not for a content's being conscious
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Tightening the experimental control defeats the aim: the better the content is matched, the harder the conscious/unconscious contrast is to sustain.
span.note: what this limits: a state-based design that matches content across conditions: the better the matching, the harder it becomes to uphold the very contrast the approach depends on
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The field states that absence of the neural marker cannot be read as absence of the phenomenon.
span.note: what this limits: a negative NCC finding in a patient: the researchers are explicit that absent thalamocortical or SMA activity cannot be taken as evidence of absence of consciousness
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A CONTROL GROUP ARGUED AWAY RATHER THAN OMITTED. Owen's case that the vegetative-state patient's sustained SMA response is voluntary rests on its duration and on its changing to order - and the author notes that this logic, if it works, makes a control group unnecessary, since ANY brain activity time-locked to the requests would show the same thing. He calls that consequence puzzling rather than wrong.

span.label: Because content-based NCC studies hold the subject's overall conscious state fixed rather than manipulating it, that presupposed conscious state remains an uncontrolled potential cause of the content's being conscious, i.e. a confound.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: What the content-based approach can legitimately identify is the neural correlate of a content being selected for conscious presentation rather than not selected, which is a different target from a content's being conscious.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same experimental method would serve researchers who care only about explicit representation and are agnostic about whether their subjects are conscious, so the method is not specifically directed at consciousness at all.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In state-based studies there is a trade-off: the more carefully conscious content is matched across conditions, the weaker the grounds for believing the two conditions still differ in being conscious versus unconscious rather than being two conscious conditions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Taking sustained, instruction-locked brain responses as evidence of consciousness makes voluntary control the criterion of consciousness, which substitutes volition for phenomenality and so changes the explanatory target.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The alternative route of inferring state consciousness from the presence of a content NCC also fails, because the content-based approach already assumes the subject is in a conscious state and therefore cannot independently establish it.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper concludes that neither the content-based nor the state-based paradigm, pursued on its own, can deliver the neural correlates of consciousness.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The remedy proposed is not to conjoin the two approaches' results but to build a new paradigm that targets the causal, mechanistic interplay between content processing and overall conscious state across contents and across conscious and unconscious state types.
